title: Build transformation pipelines
explanation:
Graphics and simulation code chains transformations: scale, then rotate, then shear. Instead of pushing every point through each step, multiply the step matrices once, remembering that the first step sits on the **right** [1]. One combined matrix then does the whole pipeline in a single product per point.

Repeating a pipeline $k$ times is the matrix power $M^k$. Areas are easy to track without moving any points: each pass scales every area by $|\det M|$ [2], so after $k$ passes the factor is $|\det M|^k$. Orientation flips on a pass exactly when that pass has a negative determinant, so an even number of flips restores it.

Debugging habit: push $\hat\imath$ and $\hat\jmath$ through the pipeline by hand and compare with the columns of your combined matrix.
keyIdeas: Pipeline 'first $B$, then $A$' is the single matrix $AB$.
$k$ repeats of a pass = $M^k$; areas scale by $|\det M|^k$.
Check a pipeline by tracking where $\hat\imath$ and $\hat\jmath$ land.

workedExample.problem: One pass rotates by $90^\circ$ counter-clockwise, $R=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, then scales by $2$, $S=2I$. Find the pass matrix, its determinant, and the area of a unit square after two passes.
steps: Rotation first, so the pass matrix is $M=SR=\begin{pmatrix}0&-2\\2&0\end{pmatrix}$.
$\det M=0\cdot0-(-2)\cdot2=4>0$: each pass multiplies area by 4 and keeps orientation.
The unit square ends with area $1\times16=16$.
workedExample.answer: $M=\begin{pmatrix}0&-2\\2&0\end{pmatrix}$, $\det M=4$; after two passes the area is $16$

pitfalls: Multiplying the step matrices in the order they are applied (left to right) instead of right to left.
Adding determinants across passes instead of multiplying them.
Using det instead of |det| for area after an orientation flip.

citations.quote: You first apply the transformation represented by the matrix on the right, then you apply the transformation represented by the matrix on the left.
So since the areas of all those tiny grid squares are being scaled by a certain amount, the area of the blob as a whole will be scaled by that amount.
